366834.title: Caterpillar maximum-centre neighbour conjecture (Hurlbert survey arXiv:2501.16144 Conjecture 39, attributed to Zhang-Ran-Huang, DAM 344 (2024) 170-178, doi 10.1016/j.dam.2023.11.035)
366834.overall_reason: The mathematics is correct and the Lean packet is technically clean. The credited content has to be the existential reading, because the literal universal statement fails trivially in range: at r = 2 it fails on Zhang-Ran-Huang's own P^{4,1}, where mu = 4 and r <= mu/2. The 11-vertex witness lies outside the Holroyd-Talbot range r <= mu/2, the original ZRH wording (their Conjecture 4.1) is unread, and the in-range strengthening is not yet formalized. Recommend upgrading the Lean endpoint before acceptance (see recommended_lean_target).

A_source_fidelity.survey_text: 'If T is a caterpillar, r >= 1, and z is a maximum r-center, then the neighbor of z has maximum degree.' This is verbatim identical in survey v1 (27 Jan 2025), v2, v3 and v4 (22 Aug 2026), fetched and compared. The MathDB record paraphrases it faithfully.
A_source_fidelity.context: The survey (Sec. 4) introduces the conjecture right after ZRH's result that for the caterpillar P^{k,t} every pendant neighbour of v_2 or v_{k-1} (vertices of maximum degree t+2) is a maximum r-centre for all r and t. The survey defines maximum r-centres with no range on r, and defines HK and r-HK for all r. There is no r <= mu/2 restriction anywhere in that subsection.
A_source_fidelity.original_ZRH: UNREAD. ScienceDirect abstract page: 403 on a single attempt, not retried. zbMATH Open 1529.05125: review text withheld for licensing reasons (keywords: independent set, star, caterpillar, center). OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar: no abstract, closed access, no arXiv version. Citing paper Zhang-Zhang, Disc. Math. 2026 (doi 10.1016/j.disc.2026.115113): no arXiv version, body unread. A search-engine snippet of the publisher abstract says the conjecture is 'Conjecture 4.1' and that the paper determines centres for three types of caterpillars. That snippet is unverified secondary text.
A_source_fidelity.defect: The literal statement is ill-posed. 'The neighbor of z' presupposes a leaf. At r = 1 every vertex is a maximum centre. At r = 2, |I^2_v| = n - 1 - deg v, so every leaf is a maximum 2-centre. Exact check: on ZRH's own P^{4,1} (mu = 4, r = 2 = mu/2) the leaves at v_1 and v_4 are maximum 2-centres adjacent to degree-2 vertices, while Delta = 3. So the universal reading fails in range on the authors' own example. The only non-trivial reading is existential: some maximum r-centre is a leaf whose neighbour has degree Delta. That reading is consistent with the P^{k,t} theorem that motivated it.

B_mathematics.own_verification: scripts/cat_verify.py cross-checks two independent methods: brute-force enumeration of independent r-sets, and independence-polynomial tree DP. mu is computed by brute force (n <= 19) and by an exact independent-domination tree DP, and the two agree.
B_mathematics.witness_11: Leaf counts (1,2,1,0,2), n = 11, alpha = 7, mu = 4 (exact), Delta = 4 (at v1 only). Stars at r = 6: [7,1,2,12,0,8,13,13,12,14,14], matching the lane. Maximum 6-centres are exactly {9,10}, whose neighbour v4 has degree 3. Both the universal and the existential readings fail, at r = 6 < alpha = 7 but r = 6 > mu/2 = 2.
B_mathematics.minimality: Exhaustive own search (scripts/cat_search.py ... any): there is no existential failure with 3 <= r <= alpha for n <= 10. At n = 11 the only failure is (1,2,1,0,2) at r = 6, up to reversal. This confirms the lane's minimality claim.
B_mathematics.family: Leaf counts (m-1,m,m-1,0,m) at r = 5 fail the existential reading for every m = 3..10 (exact, brute force and DP agree). mu = m + 3 exactly, by tree DP, by brute force for m <= 4, and by hand: a spine vertex outside S forces all its leaves into S, and the cheapest spine pattern is {v0,v2,v4}, costing 3 + m. alpha = 4m - 1 and Delta = m + 2 (at v1).
B_mathematics.root_diagnostic_correction: The root note's 'm = 7 (35 vertices) ... neighbour degree 9 < Delta = 10' mixes two family members. m = 7 has 31 vertices, mu = 10, Delta = 9, maximum 5-centres = the 7 leaves of v4 (star 18106; neighbour degree 8). m = 8 has 35 vertices, mu = 11, Delta = 10, neighbour degree 9. Both are in range (2r = 10 <= mu). The first in-range member of the family is m = 7 (31 vertices).
B_mathematics.in_range_existence: YES. The existential reading fails within r <= mu(T)/2, for example (6,7,6,0,7) with n = 31 and r = 5 = mu/2. The smallest in-range failures found are n = 28: (1,4,6,5,0,6) at r = 5 (mu = 10, Delta = 8, maximum centres = the 6 leaves of v5, neighbour degree 7, star 10857), and (3,4,5,4,1,5) at r = 6 (mu = 12). Both are brute-force cross-checked (scripts/cat_crosscheck.py). Search coverage: exhaustive over all caterpillars with n <= 23 (no in-range failure); n = 24..27 checked only for spine length <= 7 (none); n = 28..31 for spine length <= 6 (67 failures). The minimum in-range order is therefore 24..28, not fully settled.
B_mathematics.other_readings: r <= alpha/2: the 31- and 28-vertex witnesses qualify (alpha = 27 and 23). 3 <= r < alpha: the 11-vertex witness qualifies. Leaf-centre readings ('if z is a leaf maximum centre ...', or 'some leaf maximum centre ...'): covered, since all maximum centres in every witness are leaves adjacent to non-maximum-degree vertices.

C_lean.audit: Own audit fresh/RevAuditCaterpillarCenter.lean covers all 52 constants of module CaterpillarCenter, generated ones included (10 def, 42 theorem). Every def and theorem has a body; there are no axiom, opaque or quot declarations; nothing is unsafe, partial, implemented_by or extern; no value contains sorry; transitive axioms are within {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}. The token scan finds no sorry, admit, axiom, native_decide, ofReduceBool, set_option or run_cmd in the proof file.
C_lean.fidelity: IsCaterpillar (a tree plus a path dominating every vertex), starSize (card of {s | IsNIndepSet r s and v in s}) and IsMaxCenter (maximum over all vertices) are faithful. CaterpillarCenterConjecture is the literal universal reading: its negation is the exact negation of the MathDB statement, but it is trivially refutable at r = 2 and carries no significance by itself. CaterpillarCenterConjectureWeak (exists a maximum centre z with some neighbour of degree maxDegree) is the strongest existential form, and its negation is the meaningful theorem. Neither endpoint imposes r <= mu/2.

D_prior_art.evidence: Survey v4 (22 Aug 2026) still lists Conjecture 39 and Problem (b), 'Where are the maximum r-centers for caterpillars?'. Estrugo-Pastine (DAM 2021) predates ZRH and only proves caterpillars are HK. arXiv 2601.16953 (Jan 2026, perfect r-ary trees) was read and does not address it. Semantic Scholar lists only two citers of ZRH: the survey, and Zhang-Zhang (Disc. Math. 2026), whose body was not read (paywalled). Two web searches found no refutation. Registry screens found nothing.
D_prior_art.residual: Zhang-Zhang 2026 body and the ZRH original are unread.

reasons: It refutes a conjecture published in DAM 2024 and listed as open in a 2025/2026 survey (Springer chapter doi 10.1007/978-3-032-18810-6_10). It is not a known result or a routine corollary.

It is NOT a wording correction, provided the credited theorem is the existential reading: no maximum r-centre has any neighbour of maximum degree. The literal-universal failure alone is a wording defect and would merit zero credit.
The witness is small and computer-found (11 vertices), and the mechanism is a plain finite count. That makes it modest rather than deep.
Robustness to an unread original that might restrict r to r <= mu/2 (the Holroyd-Talbot range) requires the in-range witness. That witness exists (n = 28 or 31) but is not yet formalized.

366834.scope_reading: The strongest natural non-trivial reading: for every caterpillar T and every r with 1 <= r (equivalently 1 <= r <= alpha, since stars are empty beyond alpha), some maximum r-centre is a leaf adjacent to a vertex of maximum degree. The refutation should negate the weaker hypothesis 'some maximum r-centre has some neighbour of maximum degree', and should hold with 2r <= mu(T).

recommended_lean_target.statement: theorem not_caterpillarCenterConjectureInRange : ¬ (∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (T : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel T.Adj], IsCaterpillar T → ∀ r : ℕ, 1 ≤ r → (∀ s : Finset V, T.IsIndepSet (s : Set V) → (∀ t : Finset V, T.IsIndepSet (t : Set V) → s ⊆ t → s = t) → 2 * r ≤ s.card) → ∃ z : V, IsMaxCenter T r z ∧ ∃ w : V, T.Adj z w ∧ T.degree w = T.maxDegree)
recommended_lean_target.notes: The mu hypothesis is stated without defining min: every maximal independent set has at least 2r elements. This single endpoint implies not_caterpillarCenterConjectureWeak and not_caterpillarCenterConjecture. Keep the existing 11-vertex theorems as the minimal-order statement.
recommended_lean_target.witness_options: (1,4,6,5,0,6) with n = 28, r = 5, maximum centres = the 6 leaves of v5, star 10857 vs 10853 for the leaves of v2, the unique vertex of degree Delta = 8 (margin 4); v5 has degree 7. Or (6,7,6,0,7) with n = 31, r = 5, star 18106 for the leaves of v4 (degree 8) vs 18091 for the leaves of v1 (degree Delta = 9; margin 15).
recommended_lean_target.feasibility: Raw kernel decide over the Finset definition is NOT feasible. Probe fresh/Probe3.lean, counting a single 3-star on the 28-vertex graph (3,276 subsets), exceeded the 6 GiB private-RSS cap after 28.6 s and was killed (logs/probe3.receipt.json). A proved counting method is required: either a computable List.rec independent-set counter with a correctness bridge to the Finset card, or a structural decomposition |I^r_z| = i_{r-1}(T - N[z]) with a forest product formula. The mu >= 10 hypothesis has a short structural proof (case split on the spine vertices; each spine vertex outside S forces its leaves into S). Estimated effort: moderate, a few hundred lines, medium risk.

objections: The literal MathDB statement is trivially false (r = 1, r = 2; in range on P^{4,1}). Credit must rest on the existential reading, and root must rule that this is the intended exact scope.

The original ZRH Conjecture 4.1 is unread. It could carry hypotheses (for example r <= mu/2, or a caterpillar subclass) that the survey dropped. The in-range witness covers the mu/2 case; a subclass restriction cannot be excluded.
The 11-vertex witness (r = 6, mu = 4) is far outside r <= mu/2, so on its own it does not address the Holroyd-Talbot range.
The root diagnostic mislabels the family member (m = 7 has 31 vertices; 35 vertices is m = 8). Both are valid in-range counterexamples.
Significance is modest: an 11-vertex computer search against a recent and loosely worded conjecture.
next_actions: Formalize the in-range endpoint above on the 28-vertex (or 31-vertex) witness with a proved counting method; kernel decide is infeasible.
Root: rule whether the existential in-range refutation counts as resolving MathDB 366834 in its exact scope, given that the record's literal wording is trivially false.
If lawful public access to ZRH Conjecture 4.1 appears (author page, thesis, open repository), record its exact hypotheses before acceptance.

366371.title: Keller-Petrov majorization characterization conjecture (Ordinal spaces, arXiv:2412.17391v1 Conjecture 7.4; published Acta Math. Hungar. 160 (2020) 119-152, doi 10.1007/s10474-019-00972-z, online 5 Sep 2019)
366371.overall_reason: The source fidelity, mathematics and Lean are all correct and faithful. The witness is a genuine counterexample in the range n > 5 that the source explicitly leaves open. Significance is real but modest, and is qualified by the classical measurement-theory expectation.

A_source_fidelity.checked: Definition 1.1 (i)-(vii), (7.1)-(7.3), the definition of I_n (k in N+, nondecreasing tuples with repeats), Definition 7.1, Proposition 7.2, Conjecture 7.4 and Theorem 7.5 were read in the arXiv HTML. The Lean IsOrdinalSpace matches (i)-(vii) field by field (ax_v and ax_vi use 'not >' for 'in {<,=}'). EmbeddableInLine matches (7.1)-(7.3) with d = |s - t|. Prec and Sim use one permutation of {1..k} with the same k on both sides, pieces (i_{l-1}, i_l) and (j_{pi(l)-1}, j_{pi(l)}), and 'not (7.4)' for that same pi. HasMajorization quantifies over all k > 0 and all pairs of monotone tuples, for the given enumeration. MajorizationConjecture says: exists a bijective enumeration with majorization, implies embeddable.
A_source_fidelity.one_vs_all_enumerations: The source's hypothesis is existential ('let there exist an enumeration ... satisfying the majorization property'). The Lean conjecture takes e as a universally quantified hypothesis, which is equivalent. The witness uses the identity enumeration.
A_source_fidelity.not_74_reading: The two possible readings of 'but not (7.4)' are 'not all equal under this pi' and 'not (I ~ J)'. I checked them literally for k <= 4 and they are equivalent; in general they agree because delta is a total preorder (a termwise <= matching plus multiset equality forces termwise equality). So the Lean choice is harmless.
A_source_fidelity.n_gt_5_phrase: The source says sufficiency is open 'if n > 5', but proves it only for n <= 4, so n = 5 is unaddressed (probably a slip for n >= 5). The witness has n = 6, inside the explicitly open range under either reading.
A_source_fidelity.publication_note: The lane and MathDB treat this as a 2024 arXiv paper. It is in fact a 2019/2020 Acta Math. Hungarica article (public Springer landing page and OpenAlex metadata). The published full text was not read: only institutional access exists, which is not public, so it was not used. That the arXiv v1 matches the published Conjecture 7.4 is assumed, not verified.

B_mathematics.own_verification: scripts/ord_verify.py. The ranking reproduces the Lean D matrix exactly. Axioms (i)-(vii) are checked by brute force over all 6^6 sextuples. Definition 7.1 is checked literally, with explicit permutations and repeated indices, for k = 1..4: 441, 3136, 15876 and 63504 chain pairs, with 195, 1192, 5211 and 18733 strict-majorized pairs, and 0 violations. All k are covered by an exact characterization: each chain is its repeat-free reduction plus zero pieces, and the existence of a dominating permutation is equivalent to termwise dominance of sorted values, which is invariant under zero padding. All 63 x 63 pairs of reduced lists were checked with 0 violations. Threshold-count dominance equals sorted-value dominance for every pair, which confirms the lane's reduction (the heart of the Lean finite check).
B_mathematics.non_embeddability: {0,5} is the unique largest pair, and D(0,x) is increasing for x = 1..4, so any embedding is order 0<1<2<3<4<5 up to reflection. The five comparisons D(2,3)<D(3,4), D(1,2)<D(2,4), D(0,1)<D(1,3), D(1,4)<D(4,5) and D(3,5)<D(0,2) all hold. Their gap coefficients are [1,2,2,2,1] on both sides, so their sum is a strict inequality between identical sums. Contradiction.
B_mathematics.not_reverified: The lane's n = 5 'no counterexample' minimality scan (LP via scipy) was not independently reproduced. It is a diagnostic only.

Every def and theorem has a body; there are no axiom or opaque declarations; nothing is unsafe, partial, implemented_by or extern; no sorry; axioms are within {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}. The finite check uses decide +kernel, with no native_decide or ofReduceBool.

The finite check okB runs over sublists of [0..5] (64 x 64, including the empty list, which okB handles) and thresholds t = 1..15. D_le guarantees every piece value lies in [1, 15] except 0 for degenerate pieces.

D_prior_art.evidence: The conjecture has been public since 2019 (Acta Math. Hungar.). Citers per Semantic Scholar: 'Echeloned Spaces' (arXiv 2312.11141, Forum Math. Sigma 2025; abstract and text read: metrizability, Fraisse limits and Ramsey property, nothing on line embeddability or majorization), and 'Towards Ordinal Data Science' (2023, position paper). OpenAlex cited_by_count = 1. An extended web search found no refutation. arXiv lists only v1 (Dec 2024).
D_prior_art.residual: The classical unidimensional ordinal scaling and absolute-difference-structure literature (Krantz-Luce-Suppes-Tversky Vol. 1 Ch. 4; Coombs unfolding; Robinsonian matrices; Fishburn) was not searched body by body. An equivalent 6-point example could exist there under different terminology, but a match to this exact chain-majorization condition would be needed.

reasons: Scott (1964) and Krantz-Luce-Suppes-Tversky show that finite representability is equivalent to the full family of cancellation conditions (a Farkas or LP duality argument), and that no bounded-order subfamily suffices. Majorization is not bounded-order: k is unbounded. It is a restricted-shape subfamily, in which each side must tile a single interval by a chain in the enumeration order. So its insufficiency does not follow from those theorems and needs an explicit example. It is not a routine corollary.

The phenomenon is expected in spirit. It is analogous to Kraft-Pratt-Seidenberg (1959), which showed that de Finetti's axioms are insufficient for qualitative probability on 5 atoms. Experts in measurement theory would likely have predicted failure.

It resolves the authors' explicitly stated open question for n > 5, and is minimal-adjacent: sufficiency is proved for n <= 4, and the lane's n = 5 scan is diagnostic. It is not an endpoint, domain or wording correction, and not a parameter instance.
The witness is computer-found and the certificate is a 5-term linear combination, so the depth is modest.

366371.scope_reading: Exactly the source's Conjecture 7.4: for all finite ordinal spaces, if some enumeration has the majorization property (all k >= 1, nondecreasing tuples with repeats, permutations), then the space embeds in R^1. No narrowing is needed.

recommended_lean_target.statement: OrdinalSpaces366371.not_majorizationConjecture : ¬ MajorizationConjecture (the existing endpoint), together with witness.
recommended_lean_target.notes: This is adequate as is. An optional strengthening, failure for every n >= 6 by adding far-away points, is not required for MathDB 366371.

objections: Significance is qualified by the classical measurement-theory expectation that restricted cancellation families fail. Root should weigh this.
The source is a 2019/2020 journal paper, not a 2024 preprint. The published wording was not verified against the arXiv v1 (institutional access only, not used).
The source's 'n > 5' versus the proved 'n <= 4' leaves n = 5 formally unaddressed. The witness avoids the issue (n = 6).
Prior-art search of the classical scaling literature is bounded.
next_actions: Root significance ruling, given the measurement-theory caveat.
Optional: independently reproduce the n = 5 minimality diagnostic with an exact rational LP if minimality is to be claimed in a paper.
